_notes: Arathi Highlands quest pass (2026-11-01). Generated by tools/build_arathi_quests.py - do not hand-edit text here.

quests.title: The Road Is the Camp
quests.description:
Refuge Pointe holds a road. That is the whole of it - there is no fort here, there is a human ruin with tents in it and a road running past, and the road is the reason anyone is standing in the ruin.

The Syndicate works the road. Not a raid, not a war: a steady, patient skim off everything that moves along it.
quests.accept_text:
You will not find a camp to burn. They do not have one on the road - they come down off the high ground, take what is loose, and go back up.

So you do it the slow way. Walk the road, and every time one of them comes down off the grass, make it the last time. Ten should get the message to whoever is counting on the other end.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ten, and the adders, which nobody asked you for and everybody will thank you for.

The road will stay quiet for about nine days. I have measured it. That is not cynicism, that is a supply schedule.

quests.title: Wide Country
quests.description:
Scout Hollowfoot's standing complaint about this moor is that it looks empty and is not. It is simply very good at being wide: everything on it is further away than it appears, and a thing that is two hours away looks like a thing that is twenty minutes away right up until you have walked for two hours.

He wants a second pair of feet to agree with him about the distances.
quests.accept_text:
The High Moor, the Lowland Oaks, and the gap in the wall. Walk all three and do not ride.

I am not asking you to find anything. I am asking you to find out how long it takes, because every man I have lost up here was lost to thinking he could get somewhere before dark.
quests.turn_in_text:
Now you know. The oaks are further than they look and the wall is further than that.

That is the single most useful thing anyone learns on this moor, and it cannot be told. It has to be walked.

quests.title: The Gap
quests.description:
Warden Ada Rook has stood at the gap in Thoradin's Wall for a year and a half. The arch above her is Arathor stonework three thousand years old and the thing she has actually been doing is counting: how many came through, from which side, and what they were carrying.

The number for the first year was zero. It is not zero any more, and a good deal of what comes through now is Syndicate.
quests.accept_text:
They cross at night and they cross in threes, and every one of them is carrying a slip with a number on it.

I want four of those slips. Not because I think they will tell me anything - because I have been counting for eighteen months and I would like, just once, to see somebody else's count.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four slips and all four agree with my book.

Eighteen months I have been doing this and it turns out I have been doing it correctly. I did not expect that to feel like anything. It does.

quests.title: What the Kites Find
quests.description:
Shepherd Ogrin was an axethrower and is now the man who keeps the highland stag herd off the road, which he will explain to you at length if you let him.

His actual problem is the carrion kites. They have learned that the road produces bodies, and a kite that has learned that stops waiting for one.
quests.accept_text:
A kite is a carrion bird. It is supposed to turn up second. These ones have started turning up first and that is a thing a bird should not be able to decide to do.

Thin them. And the fleshrippers while you are out there, because the rippers are the reason the kites learned.
quests.turn_in_text:
The herd came down to the low grass on its own this morning. First time since spring.

They know. People think a stag is stupid. A stag is not stupid, a stag is busy.

quests.title: Adder Season
quests.description:
Quartermaster Horg requisitions for a garrison of forty and is supplied for a garrison of twelve, and the gap between those two numbers is filled by whatever he can make here.

Antivenin is top of the list. Moor adders come up out of the grass onto warm road stone at dusk and the camp has had four bites this month.
quests.accept_text:
Eight glands and whatever bruiseweed you can pull on the way. The weed grows along the road cuts - you will walk past it whether you are looking or not.

And keep the bruiseweed. I need to see it, not take it off you. I am not robbing people who do me favours, that is the Syndicate's business model.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is the camp covered until the weather turns.

Four bites this month and nobody died, and the reason nobody died is a shelf. People think a quartermaster is a clerk. A quartermaster is a shelf with opinions.

quests.title: Go'Shek Still Brings It In
quests.description:
Nalla Deeps has been looking at Go'Shek Farm for a month and the thing that interests her is not that the Syndicate took it. It is that the farm is still working.

The fields are cut on time. The barns are not empty. Somebody is doing the farming, and somebody else is buying what comes off it, and neither of those people is a bandit.
quests.accept_text:
Every watchman on that farm carries a field tally, because a man guarding a harvest has to know how much harvest there is.

Get me five. I want to see the yield. A yield tells you the acreage, the acreage tells you the labour, and the labour will tell me something I have been wrong about.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four hundred bushels off ground that size needs thirty people working it, and the Syndicate has nine men on that farm.

So the farmers are still there. They never left. They are working for whoever is standing in the house, which is what farmers have always done, and I owe them a better question than the one I came with.

quests.title: Who Buys the Grain
quests.description:
The farm works. The farmers stayed. That leaves the part Nalla actually cares about, which is the money: four hundred bushels a season does not get eaten by nine bandits in a farmhouse.

It is going somewhere. It is being paid for. And whoever is paying for it is doing business with the Syndicate in quantity, on paper, from somewhere with a market.
quests.accept_text:
The prowlers run the roads and the shadowmages run the house, and the paper will be on one of the two. My money is the house.

Bring me a contract. One is enough. I do not need the whole ledger, I need one name at the bottom of one page.
quests.turn_in_text:
Signed, countersigned, and the buyer's mark is a Hillsbrad merchant house with a charter older than the Syndicate.

They are not fencing it. They are not laundering it. They are buying grain from the people holding the farm, at a fair price, because grain is grain. I have been chasing a crime and I have found a supply chain.

quests.title: The Overseer's Books
quests.description:
There is one more thing on that farm that Nalla wants and cannot get at: the overseer's own room, in the main house, where the books that are not field tallies are kept.

She is not asking you to kill the man. She is asking you to be in that room for long enough that the Syndicate has to move its paper somewhere else, which is the only kind of damage that lasts.
quests.accept_text:
Get inside the house and be seen doing it. Take three leaves out of whatever is on that desk - any three - and leave the rest on the floor.

They will move everything within a week and moving a ledger is when a ledger gets lost. I have waited a month for one page. I can wait a week for the rest of it to fall out of a cart.
quests.turn_in_text:
Three leaves and the house in uproar. Good.

The farmers get to keep farming either way, which was never going to change and was never the point. The point is that somebody in Alterac now has to explain a gap in the accounts. Let them.

quests.title: The Hollow
quests.description:
There are Witherbark in a fold of ground on the west side of the moor, and Scout Hollowfoot's report on them is one line long: they were here first and they are not going anywhere.

What has changed is that they have started coming out, which they did not do for the first eighteen months, and a troll village that changes its habits is a village that has had something happen to it.
quests.accept_text:
I want to know what changed and I am not going to find out by asking, because the last two people who tried are part of the reason I am asking you.

Go in far enough that they commit to defending it. What they defend hardest tells you what they are worried about, and that is the report I actually need.
quests.turn_in_text:
The hollow, not the village. They gave up the outer camps and went hard for the hollow itself.

So there is something in the fold of that ground that matters more than their own houses, and now I know where to look.

quests.title: What the Harbinger Hears
quests.description:
The thing the Witherbark are defending is in the deepest part of the hollow, and the Witherbark have a harbinger standing over it.

Hollowfoot has one piece of hard information: trolls bury a listening charm at the edge of a camp, facing out, to hear what is coming. Every charm in that hollow is facing IN.
quests.accept_text:
Six charms, and I want them lifted where they lie so I can see which way each one faced. Do not go for the harbinger. She is not the question.

The question is why a village would spend a year listening to itself.
quests.turn_in_text:
All six facing in. Every one.

They are not watching the moor. They are watching something that is already inside the hollow with them, and they have been doing it since about the time we arrived. I am going to need to think about whether those two facts are related.

quests.title: The Crags
quests.description:
Boulder'gor sits in the crags north of the camp and is the near end of an ogre problem that gets worse the further east you go. Commander Raskal does not have the people to deal with it and says so without apology.

What she needs is a count, and a count means going up there.
quests.accept_text:
Get up into the crags and come back able to tell me how many. Not an impression - a number, or the closest thing to one you can stand behind.

Kill what comes at you on the way. That is not the task, that is the weather.
quests.turn_in_text:
More than I hoped and fewer than I feared, which is the answer I get to every question on this moor.

They are not massing. They are living there. That is a thing we can leave alone for another season and I intend to.

quests.title: The Pit
quests.description:
There is a hole in the floor of the Boulder'gor cave with a lip built around it, and the ogres fight in it. The one who has never lost calls himself the Pit Chief.

Raskal would happily leave the crags alone for a season. She cannot leave this alone, because two of the bodies the kites found on the road last month had been in that pit first.
quests.accept_text:
He counts out loud. Our scouts have heard him from outside the cave mouth.

The number he shouts is much higher than the number of ogres in that hold, and the difference is people off my road. Go down there and make the counting stop.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then that is finished.

I am not going to pretend it was strategy. There are forty things on this moor more dangerous than one ogre in a hole, and I sent you after the one that had our people's names in his mouth.

quests.title: The Claim
quests.description:
Antiquarian Vesh wants to be clear about something before you go anywhere near Stromgarde: the Syndicate's claim to that keep is not a weak claim or a disputed claim. It is an invented one.

They are Alterac nobility who lost Alterac. Stromgarde was never theirs. They walked into an empty ruin three years ago and started issuing writs about it, and the writs are beautifully done.
quests.accept_text:
Get inside the outer ward and bring me four of their writs. They post them. On walls. In a keep nobody else lives in.

I want them for the archive and I want them because a forgery that good is a historical document in its own right, and in two hundred years somebody is going to believe it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at the seal work. Look at the HAND. Whoever is doing these was trained properly in a chancery that no longer exists.

That is the saddest thing on this moor and I include the barrow.

quests.title: The Gate That Has Not Opened
quests.description:
The outer gate of Stromgarde Keep has not been opened in three years. There is a man behind it whose entire function is to not open it, and he is still being paid.

Commander Raskal's interest is simpler than the Antiquarian's. The keep overlooks her road, and she would like to know what is in it.
quests.accept_text:
There is one way in and it is through him. I have had two scouts look at that wall and both came back with the same word, which was 'no'.

So go through the gate. Take the ward with it - the watch on that outer yard is thick and you will not get a second approach once they know you can get in.
quests.turn_in_text:
Open. Three years and it is open, and the hinge did not even complain much.

Eleven keys on his belt, and four of the doors they open are not standing any more. He was guarding a building that has mostly fallen down. I have no idea what to do with that.

quests.title: The Evening Office
quests.description:
There is a chapel in Stromgarde Keep with no roof on it, and somebody has read the evening office in it every evening for three years.

Vesh has had this from two separate scouts and does not know what to do with it either. The Syndicate is a protection racket with good handwriting. It is not a thing that holds vigils.
quests.accept_text:
I want her book. Not her - her book, and if there is a way to come back with the one and not the other I would take it, and there will not be.

She is in a roofless room reading to nobody in a keep full of thieves, and whatever else that is, it is the only honest thing left in that building.
quests.turn_in_text:
Every evening. Three years. The last entry is this week.

She was not keeping it for the Syndicate. She was keeping it for Stromgarde, and Stromgarde has been dead longer than she was alive. Put that on the shelf next to the forgeries. They belong together.

quests.title: The Third Claimant
quests.description:
The man sitting in Stromgarde's hall styles himself Lord Falconcrest and has had the keep's arms re-engraved with his own, badly, by his own hand.

Two others claimed that hall before him. He does not mention them by name and neither does anybody else, which tells you what happened to them.
quests.accept_text:
He has a duelling sword and a court to use it in, except there is no court, there are nine bandits and a woman reading in the rain.

He is the one giving the orders that put bodies on my road. Everything else in that keep is furniture. Go and finish it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Third claimant, third ending. Somebody will be fourth inside a month - that keep makes the offer to whoever walks in.

But the writs stop, the road quiets, and I get to stop writing letters about it. I will take the month.

quests.title: The Stair Under the Keep
quests.description:
This is the thing Antiquarian Vesh has wanted since the day she arrived.

Stromgarde is a ruin with a ruin under it. There is an undercroft beneath the throne apse that is older than the keep standing on top of it - marble where everything above is dressed stone - and the Syndicate has been living over it for three years without ever finding the stair.
quests.accept_text:
The knock-through is behind the throne. You will not find it from the hall, you will find it from the apse, and you will find it because the floor sounds wrong.

There is something down there and it has been down there the entire time. I want the coffer seal and I want to know what Arathor thought was worth sealing, and I am aware those are two questions and that I am only going to get one of them answered.
quests.turn_in_text:
Arathor's own seal on a coffer, and no record anywhere of what went into it.

They sealed it and then did not write down why, which is not carelessness - that is a decision. Somebody three thousand years ago decided the safest record was no record.

I have the seal. I am going to stop there, and I would like it noted that stopping is not something I do.

quests.title: The Refuge Road
quests.description:
Runner Keska does Refuge Pointe to Hammerfall and back twice a week on foot, because wyverns are for officers. She is the only person in the region who has walked the whole road in both directions this month.

It has got worse. She wants that written down by somebody who is not her, because she has reported it twice and been told she is tired.
quests.accept_text:
The maulers have come down off the north shelf onto the road itself, which they did not do in spring. And there are the stone things - the sentinels - standing on the verge where they used to stand in the circles.

Walk it with me in mind. Clear what is on it. Then they can tell YOU that you are tired.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ten maulers and six of the stone ones, and the road is a road again for about a fortnight.

I am not going to say I told them so. I am going to carry this report myself and put it in the Overlord's hand and stand there while he reads it.

quests.title: Carry It to the Pointe
quests.description:
Keska's road report is written and she cannot deliver it, because delivering it means two days she does not have and the next supply run leaves in the morning.

Refuge Pointe needs to know what is on the road before they send anything down it.

objectives.label: Put Keska's road report in Commander Raskal's hand

quests.accept_text:
Everything on that road, where it is, and what time of day it moves. Two years of it, in one page, because one page is what a commander reads.

Give it to Raskal herself. Not the quartermaster - she will file it, and it has been filed enough.
quests.turn_in_text:
Hour by hour. Two years of a woman walking the same road paying attention.

I have had staff officers hand me less than this. Tell her the Pointe owes her a wyvern seat and that I will be the one arguing for it.

on_accept.name: Keska's Road Report
on_accept.description: One page. Everything on that road, where it is and what time of day it moves, two years of it, in a hand that has been writing on her knee at the side of it.

quests.title: Good Growing
quests.description:
Herbalist Nahto Greenhoof's complaint about Hammerfall is that everyone in it is looking at the ogres.

The ogres will still be there next season. So will the basin, which has the best growing ground in the region running down its middle, and which nobody has surveyed because it is not a threat.
quests.accept_text:
Liferoot in the wet ground down the middle, kingsblood up where it is dry. Pull both and keep both - I want to see what the basin gives, not take it off you.

And the elk. I am sorry about the elk. They have found the liferoot too and there is not enough of it for both of us this year.
quests.turn_in_text:
Liferoot that size, this far north, in this soil.

The basin is better ground than Hillsbrad and nobody in this hold knows it. I am going to tell them. They are going to be looking at the ogres.

quests.title: Four Circles, One Line
quests.description:
Scholar Innik Barrowmouth has a map of the basin with four stone circles on it and a line drawn through all four.

The line is the trunk road. Which means either somebody built a road through four ancient monuments by coincidence, or the road is older than anyone who has ever walked it. He would like to stop being the only person who finds this interesting.
quests.accept_text:
Stand in all four. In order, west to east, and in each one look back the way you came.

You will see it on the third. On the fourth you will not be able to stop seeing it, and then you will understand why I have been in this basin for a year.
quests.turn_in_text:
You saw it. Everyone sees it on the third.

Four circles on one sightline, and the sightline is a road that Arathor paved and did not lay out. They inherited it. The first human empire in the world built its highway on top of somebody else's survey and there is no record of whose.

quests.title: The Bound Ones
quests.description:
There are stone figures standing in and around the circles. They do not move while you watch them and they are not in the same place twice.

Innik calls them Bound Sentinels because that is what the Arathor inscription calls them, and the inscription is the only thing anyone has that was written by somebody who knew.
quests.accept_text:
Five cores. They have a stone at the centre and it is not the same stone as the rest of them - it is ring stone, off the circles, and that is a fact I would like five of rather than one.

And go back to the fourth ring afterwards. Three of those circles are quiet. The fourth is not, and I want you to have the cores in your hand when you stand in it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ring stone. All five. They are made OF the circles - somebody took the monuments apart to make the guards that stand around the monuments.

That is a closed loop and I do not like it. It means whoever did it was not protecting the rings. They were feeding them.

quests.title: Ask Them First
quests.description:
High Envoy Tamka Stillwater has asked the Boulderfist twice to stop taking the standing stones down for wall rock. Twice is not enough times to have asked.

Everybody in Hammerfall thinks this is a waste of a third ask. The Envoy's position is that the third ask is the one that makes the fourth thing legitimate, and that she is not going to be the tauren who skipped it.

objectives.label: Carry the Envoy's word to Boulderfist Hall

quests.accept_text:
A carved stone. They will not read a letter and they will not take a messenger seriously, but a thing with work in it, put down at the mouth of their hold, is understood by everyone who has ever been handed one.

Set it down where it will be seen. Do not go in. Do not start anything. Walk out the way you came in and let it sit there.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then it is asked, properly, three times, and anybody who wants to say we did not try can be shown the record.

I do not expect an answer. That is not the same as not expecting one, and the difference between those two things is the whole of my office.

on_accept.name: The Envoy's Parley Stone
on_accept.description: Slate, a hand's width across, carved on both faces. The work in it is the message - nobody is meant to read it, they are meant to see how long it took.

quests.title: The Answer
quests.description:
The parley stone came back. It was returned to Hammerfall's gate in four pieces, during the night, by somebody who got close enough to put it down and leave.

High Envoy Stillwater has not raised her voice about it. She has asked for the pieces to be kept, and she has asked for one more thing to be confirmed before anyone does anything else.
quests.accept_text:
Go and look at the North Shelf circle. The one closest to their hold.

I want to know how much of it is still standing. Not an estimate - I want somebody who has walked the ring and counted what is left, because if there is enough of it left then this is still a conversation, and if there is not then it stopped being one before I ever arrived.
quests.turn_in_text:
Nine stones out of thirty-one.

Then it was never a conversation. I have been asking politely for a year to a people who finished answering before I got here.

Thank you for counting. Go and tell the Overlord that the Envoy withdraws her objection to his plan. He will know which plan.

quests.title: What Is in the Water
quests.description:
Apothecary Dellwyn Voss has written four reports about the Sunken Mere and Undercity has acknowledged receipt of three.

The mere is shallow, warm and standing, which is ordinary. What is not ordinary is that it is full, in a basin with no inflow worth the name, and that the things coming out of it are getting larger.
quests.accept_text:
Six bladders, intact, and intact is the word that matters - they rupture if you are careless and what is inside them is the entire sample.

I am not asking you to be brave. I am asking you to be slow. Bravery has cost me two couriers and no data.
quests.turn_in_text:
Freshwater organisms with a salt-gland. In a basin eighty miles from the sea.

That is not adaptation, that is the wrong animal in the wrong water, and there is only one thing in the last three years that moves animals into water they did not evolve in. I am going to write a fifth report.

quests.title: The Shallow Warm Full Place
quests.description:
The fifth report needs the middle of the mere, and the middle of the mere is where whatever is doing the breeding sits.

Voss is explicit that he does not want it killed. He wants it LOOKED at, from close enough to count, which he concedes is a harder thing to ask of a person than killing it would be.
quests.accept_text:
Four pearls off the bed and a good look at what is in the middle.

Freshwater pearls. In a mere. Something down there is making them and making them in rows, and I would like very much to know whether the rows mean anything or whether I am a man who has been alone with a pond for too long.
quests.turn_in_text:
Rows. Four to a row, consistently, over an area the size of this longhouse.

I am not going to speculate in writing. I am going to send Undercity the pearls and the measurements and let somebody senior to me be the one who says it out loud.

quests.title: The Village in the Basin
quests.description:
Deathguard Olen watches Hammerfall's east gate. Everything that has come through it in two years has been kobold, ogre, or a man with a very good reason.

Since the spring it has also been Witherbark, in numbers, from a village up the basin that had been keeping to itself since before the hold was built.
quests.accept_text:
They were quiet for two years and now they are not, and nobody in this hold can tell me what changed.

I am not interested in why today. Today I am interested in fewer of them arriving at my gate at four in the morning. Go up the basin and make that happen, and then we can both be curious at a reasonable hour.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quieter. Not quiet.

There is a hollow on the far side of this region where the same thing is happening to the same people, and sooner or later somebody is going to put those two reports side by side. It is not going to be me. I watch a gate.

quests.title: Boulderfist Hall
quests.description:
The Envoy has withdrawn her objection. Overlord Gath'rok's plan was never complicated: the Boulderfist hold a stone circle as their outer wall, they are taking the rest of the circles apart to thicken it, and they have now answered three asks with a broken stone at his gate.

He has waited a year to be allowed to do this properly.
quests.accept_text:
Krakk first - he is in the long hall and he is the one the rest of them watch. Then Hal'dun, who is the hold chief and who will not come out from behind the ring wall for anything.

I am not sending the garrison. A garrison takes the hold and then has to hold the hold. You go in, you end the two of them, and the rest of it stops being a problem without Hammerfall acquiring a second place to defend.
quests.turn_in_text:
Both. Good.

The Envoy wants the stones put back. I have told her that is forty men for a season and she has told me she will take forty men for a season, and I find I do not have an argument. She asked three times. I am going to say yes.

quests.title: Drywhisker Gorge
quests.description:
Prospector Thugg's position on Drywhisker is that it was a mine before the kobolds got it and it is a mine now, and the only difference is that the kobolds dug past the ore.

He wants to reopen it. Before anyone will listen to him he has to show that the seam is still there, which means samples, which means the gorge.

objectives.label: Iron out of the Drywhisker seam

quests.accept_text:
Eight of iron off the gorge face, and keep it - I want to see the grade, not own it.

The diggers work the open cut and they will come at you in threes. They are not soldiers. I want that said plainly before you go: they are miners, and we are about to argue with them about a hole.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is good iron and there is a lot of it and it is eleven feet from the surface.

They walked past this. Every day for three years, carrying spoil over a seam that would keep Hammerfall in nails for a decade, to get at something deeper. I want to know what.

quests.title: Every Candle in the Deeps
quests.description:
There is a kobold in the first gallery of Drywhisker who has never let his candle go out, and who will not let anyone else carry it.

Thugg has been told this by two different scouts and finds it the single most useful fact he has about the place. A mine run by somebody who is that frightened of the dark is a mine with a reason.
quests.accept_text:
Tallow runs the upper gallery and he runs it on wax. Every lamp hook, every niche, every stub in that level goes back to him.

Take the gallery and take him. Not because he is dangerous - because while he is lighting that level, nobody below him has to explain why they will not come up.
quests.turn_in_text:
Dipped, not woven. He had been dipping those robes his whole life.

And the upper gallery is lit by his wax and nothing else, which means when it goes out we are going to find out what the second gallery has been doing in the dark.

quests.title: The Shift Does Not End
quests.description:
Deathguard Olen has read Thugg's report and found the part Thugg skipped over.

The kobold shift in Drywhisker is still being worked. There is an overseer down there blowing a whistle and diggers are still coming when it blows, three years into a mine that stopped producing anything anyone wanted.
quests.accept_text:
I have watched a gate for two years and the thing I have learned is that people do not keep doing a job for no reason. They keep doing it because stopping is worse.

Bring me the whistle. I want to hold the object that nine hundred creatures have been obeying since before we got here.
quests.turn_in_text:
Bone, drilled, and the mouthpiece is worn through to a different colour.

They still came when it blew. I had your account of it before you handed me this and I did not believe it. They still came.

quests.title: The Warm Gallery
quests.description:
Apothecary Voss has gone through the Deathguard's notes and found one line that stops him: the deepest gallery is the warm one.

A mine gets colder as it goes down. Drywhisker does not. Something at the bottom of that mine is producing heat, and the kobolds have put their nursery next to it.
quests.accept_text:
Five shells and a look at the sump. I want the shells because a shell tells you the temperature it was laid at, and I want the sump because the sump is where the heat is coming from.

The Pick-Mother will be between you and both. I am sorry about that and I am going to ask you to do it anyway.
quests.turn_in_text:
Laid at blood heat. Eleven degrees above the rock around them.

They did not nest down there because it was safe. They nested down there because it was warm, and something has been keeping it warm since before there were kobolds in this mine.

quests.title: What They Dug Into
quests.description:
Overlord Gath'rok has the prospector's seam report, the Deathguard's whistle and the apothecary's shell temperatures on the same table, and the three of them say one thing.

The kobolds of Drywhisker walked past a decade of iron, every day, for three years, to keep digging toward something below the sump. They found it. Nothing that has come up out of that mine since is behaving like a kobold.
quests.accept_text:
I am not going to dress this up. Three of my people have been down to the sump and one came back, and what he said when he got here was that the water is not the bottom.

Go down. End it. And bring up whatever they were leaving on the floor down there, because they were leaving things on the floor, and a creature that leaves things on a floor is not mining any more.
quests.turn_in_text:
Offerings. Three of them, arranged, and arranged is a word I have been avoiding since the Envoy first used it about the pearls in the mere.

That is Drywhisker finished and it is not Arathi finished. Rest. Eat something. Then go east, and when you get to the coast find a bosun called Tidewright and tell him Hammerfall sent you.

quests.title: Four Boats and No Officer
quests.description:
Bosun Kaz Tidewright is a bosun running a shore camp, which is not a job that exists. Orgrimmar sent four boats and nobody to command them, so he took the beach and has been holding it on the assumption that somebody will eventually turn up and either promote or arrest him.

In the meantime the Bloodsail are on his shoreline.
quests.accept_text:
The cutters come along the tideline at low water, which is the only time the flats are ground at all. Four hours a day, and nobody agrees which four.

Be on the shore when they are. Twelve of them and whatever crawls up with them, and we get to keep calling this a landing instead of a mistake.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then we hold the beach for another week.

I have been writing that sentence in the log for two years. One of these days I am going to write a different one.

quests.title: Two Tides a Day
quests.description:
Salvager Pik Bronzewhistle can see wreck after wreck from where he is standing and the tide only lets you at them twice a day.

He knows which two are worth the walk. That knowledge is the entire business, and the reason he will tell you is that he has run out of days he can physically do it in.
quests.accept_text:
The flats, at low water, and do not be clever about the timing. The water comes back across the Spindrift faster than a person walks and I have watched it happen to somebody.

Every hull has a manifest tin bolted inside the stern post. Bring me what you can reach. I want to know what these ships were carrying, because this many wrecks on one archipelago is not weather.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four tins, four manifests, and three of them are the same cargo consigned to the same buyer.

These ships were not blown onto these rocks. They were coming here. Somebody was running a route into this archipelago and the route ate them.

quests.title: My Rock Now
quests.description:
There is a man living on Bothy Rock who was on a ferry three years ago. Then the water was a different water and the ferry was on a rock.

He has not asked anybody for anything in three years. He is asking now, and what he is asking for is small enough that it took him a while to work out how to say it.
quests.accept_text:
The petrels have the lee side. That was my side. I had it for two years and then there were more of them than there were of me, which is how most things end.

And bring me the down. Five bundles. It is for a mattress. I am fifty-eight years old and I have been sleeping on a folded sail since before any of you got here.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is a mattress.

I want to be clear that I am not coming in to your camp and I am not being rescued. This is my rock. I simply intend to sleep on it properly.

quests.title: They Are Not Raiding
quests.description:
Scout Vel Ashgrave's report is one sentence and the Bosun has read it four times.

The Bloodsail on this archipelago are not raiding. They are holding. A raider takes and leaves; these ones have fortified a sea cave, posted a watch on three islands and put a purser in charge of a shelf of cargo. You do not do that unless you want something that is already here.
quests.accept_text:
Three watch orders, off three different islands. I want to see whether the same hand wrote them.

If it is three captains improvising, they are squatters and we can wait them out. If it is one hand, there is a plan, and a plan has an object.
quests.turn_in_text:
One hand. All three.

So there is a plan and somebody is running it from inside that cave, and the object of it is on this archipelago somewhere. We are not the ones who turned up uninvited. We are the ones who turned up second.

quests.title: Gallowmast
quests.description:
Gallowmast Isle is the furthest out and the only one with a standing watch on open ground rather than in a hull.

Vel wants eyes on it before anyone goes into the Wrackline cave, on the grounds that walking into a held position without knowing what is behind you is how the four boats become three.
quests.accept_text:
The wrecklamps are the part I do not like. A lamp crew on a rock in a shipping lane is not a watch, it is a lure, and we already have six hulls on these flats to prove it works.

Get out to Gallowmast, see what they are lighting, and put the lamps out while you are there.
quests.turn_in_text:
A lure. They have been wrecking ships onto this archipelago deliberately for three years and salvaging them at leisure.

Which answers the Bosun's question and asks a worse one, because you do not run a wrecking operation this patient for cargo. You run it to stop anyone leaving.

quests.title: One That Floats
quests.description:
Shipwright Oona Keelsplice has been looking at a shoreline of broken hulls for two years with nothing to fix them with. Hammerfall has timber and no reason to send it; Saltspur has reason and no timber.

What she can get is what is already out there, if somebody will go and cut it off a hull at low water without drowning.
quests.accept_text:
Ten of sound timber and six fittings - bronze, off the rails and the cleats, and bronze because three years of salt has not touched it and iron is a brown stain.

Keep the timber. I need to see the grade before I plan around it. If it is all rot I would rather know now than halfway through a keel.
quests.turn_in_text:
Not rot. Two hulls' worth of sound timber lying on the flats where I could see it from the jetty the whole time.

Give me a crew and a tide and I will give you a boat. A small one. But a boat that goes where it is pointed, which is more than this landing has had since it was a landing.

quests.title: Nobody Told Them
quests.description:
Barrow-Watcher Yelza stands outside the Drowned Barrow and does not go in.

Arathor buried its eastern march in there three thousand years ago and the march is still standing its watch. They are not cursed, they are not raised, and as far as she can tell they are not angry. Nobody ever came to relieve them, so they are still on duty.
quests.accept_text:
Dey not comin' out to hunt. Dey comin' out because you on de road an' de road is deir post, an' dat is all it ever been.

I not askin' you to go in. Go up to de door an' stand where dey can see you, an' put down de ones dat come. Dat way I know how far out de post reaches, an' how many we talkin' about.
quests.turn_in_text:
Two hundred paces from de door, an' not one step past it.

Dey holdin' a line. Still. Three t'ousand years after de last person who could tell dem to stop was put in de ground behind dem.

quests.title: The Purser
quests.description:
The Bloodsail in Wrackline Hold keep books. There is a man on a dry shelf above the tideline who writes down every bolt they spend and what it was spent on, and the Bosun has decided that is the thread to pull.

A crew with a purser has an owner. Find the purser and you find out who the owner is.
quests.accept_text:
Everything they have taken off six ships went across his shelf and into his book.

I want that book more than I want him, and I am aware I am going to get both. Bring it out dry. He keeps it high up for a reason and the reason is the only thing in that cave with any sense in it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Three years of consignments and every one of them goes to the same mark.

The Bloodsail are not freelancing out here. Somebody is paying them to close this archipelago, and when I send this to Orgrimmar they are going to have to send an officer, which means I am about to be either promoted or arrested.

quests.title: She Took It From the Sea Side
quests.description:
Captain Mory Vane took Wrackline Hold from the sea side, which nobody had thought was a side.

The Bloodsail gave her a ring instead of a ship. She took a cave instead of a command, fortified it, and has held the best anchorage on the archipelago for three years with a crew who were not given anything either.
quests.accept_text:
I have no quarrel with how she got there. I have a quarrel with the fact that she is there, and that six hulls are on these flats because of a lamp crew taking her orders.

Go in off the shelf, not the water. The water is how she expects it and she has had three years to think about that.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the hold is ours, the lamps are out, and the lane is open for the first time since any of us got here.

I have written a different sentence in the log. It took two years. I am going to leave the page open on the table for a while.

quests.title: Nothing Built At All
quests.description:
The Tidewrack is the only place on this archipelago with nothing built in it. No shelf, no planking, no lamp. Sand, pearl floor and an open sump that goes down further than the cave does.

Oona wants it cleared because it is the one sheltered water on the whole coast and she cannot build a boat on a beach the tide takes twice a day.
quests.accept_text:
It grows them back. That is the thing about Brinemaw that everyone gets wrong - they think the teeth on the tideline mean something died.

Four barbed ones and the animal itself. I need that sump clear and I need it clear before the weather turns, and I am not going to be precious about how.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four teeth, all barbed, and no animal grows a barbed tooth to eat with.

I am going to build a boat in there and I am going to try not to think about what that means. Shipwrights are very good at not thinking about the bottom.

quests.title: Who Went Looking
quests.description:
There is something standing in the Tidewrack's sump holding a lantern pole.

Yelza has the history. Three years ago, when the water came up in the night and the first hulls went onto the flats, people went out to the tideline with poles and lamps to look for survivors. Some of them did not come back. The poles did.
quests.accept_text:
Everybody who drown out dere was carryin' one of somet'ing. A ring, a coin, a lock of hair. People do dat when dey goin' out on water dey not sure of.

Bring me four. I goin' to put dem on de cairn with a name on each one if I can find de name, an' dat is de only t'ing anybody has done for dem in t'ree years.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four keepsakes an' t'ree of dem I can name.

Dey went out to look for people. Dat is all dey did wrong. Go an' rest, an' den come back, because dere is one more watch on dis coast dat nobody relieved an' it is older dan dis one by a long way.

quests.title: The Door-Shield
quests.description:
The Drowned Barrow has a warden at the top of the stair carrying a shield that was a door before it was a shield.

It is not going to let anyone past and it has not let anyone past in three thousand years. Yelza has stopped calling that a haunting. She calls it a post, because that is what it is.
quests.accept_text:
You go in now. I already told you what dey are an' I not goin' to pretend dis is somet'ing else.

De warden on de stair first. Everyt'ing below it is holdin' a line dat warden is holdin' de top of, an' until dat shield come down, de rest of dem not goin' to even see you properly.
quests.turn_in_text:
De stair is open.

Marble above, limestone an' standin' water below. De empire put its best people in de dry part an' de water come up anyway, over t'ree t'ousand years, one winter at a time. Nobody plan for dat. Nobody could.

quests.title: Relieve the Watch
quests.description:
At the bottom of the Drowned Barrow, under four feet of standing water, facing the door, is the Thane of Arathor's eastern march.

He swore to hold it. The march is a drowned field with ogres walking over it, the empire that took his oath has been gone for three thousand years, and he is still at his post because nobody with the authority to relieve him has existed since before there was a Horde.
quests.accept_text:
Dere is no trick to dis an' I not goin' to invent one. He not a monster, he not cursed, an' he not goin' to listen to a troll who show up t'ree t'ousand years late wit' no standin'.

So you do it de only way it can be done. You go down dere an' you end de watch, an' you bring me his signet so dat somebody, somewhere, has de name.
quests.turn_in_text:
Aldric. Dat is de name. Dat is de whole name an' de office an' de march it was de office of.

Everybody in dis region is holdin' ground dat not deirs. De ogres, de Syndicate, your Horde, me. He de only one who was actually from here, an' he de one dey forgot to tell.

Go on. Tell your Overlord de east is quiet. It not true, but it de first time in t'ree t'ousand years it been close.
